name: MROUND
description: MROUND returns a number rounded to the nearest specified multiple.
tldr: Rounds a number to the nearest multiple of a given value.

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description: The multiple to which you want to round. Must share the sign of number.

basicExample.description: Round 10 to the nearest multiple of 3
basicExample.explanation: The multiples of 3 nearest to 10 are 9 (distance 1) and 12 (distance 2), so 9 is returned.

advancedExamples.title: Tie-breaking rounds away from zero
advancedExamples.scenario: When exactly halfway between two multiples.
advancedExamples.description: MROUND rounds a half-multiple away from zero.
advancedExamples.explanation: 7.5 is exactly between 6 and 8 (both multiples of 2); MROUND rounds away from zero to 8.

advancedExamples.title: Round to a decimal multiple
advancedExamples.scenario: Snap a value to the nearest 0.05.
advancedExamples.explanation: 0.85 and 0.90 are the nearest multiples of 0.05; 0.87 is closer to 0.85.

howItWorks: MROUND divides number by multiple, rounds that quotient to the nearest integer (rounding half away from zero), then multiplies back. number and multiple must have the same sign, or the function returns #NUM!.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: number and multiple must share the same sign; opposite signs return #NUM!.
When the value is exactly halfway between two multiples, MROUND rounds away from zero.
Results are floating-point and may show tiny rounding artifacts.

commonErrors.cause: number and multiple have opposite signs.
commonErrors.fix: Use the same sign for both arguments.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: MROUND works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: How does MROUND break ties?
faq.answer: When a value is exactly halfway between two multiples, it rounds away from zero (e.g. MROUND(7.5,2)=8).

faq.question: Why do I get #NUM!?
faq.answer: Because number and multiple have opposite signs; make them the same sign.

faq.question: What's the difference between MROUND and CEILING/FLOOR?
faq.answer: MROUND rounds to the nearest multiple; CEILING always rounds up and FLOOR always rounds down.
